name: The Wake
label: Factory Records
lede: Caesar walked out of Altered Images just before the hits, sent a Glasgow single to Rob Gretton, and spent the next six years on Factory opening for New Order, with Bobby Gillespie on bass for the first stretch.

eras.title: From Altered Images to Stockport
eras.text: Caesar (Gerard McInulty) had written Altered Images' first single and left before they got famous. His new band found few gigs in Glasgow, so it pressed its own 45 and pointed it at Manchester, where New Order's manager was listening.

years.src: Factory Benelux: The Wake · Wikipedia: The Wake
years.h: Caesar quits Altered Images and starts the Wake in Glasgow
years.p: Caesar had played guitar on two [[John Peel|e4dec348-ad10-43b6-a2b1-c22aab890675]] sessions with [[Altered Images|318d3337-7ca5-49af-aa94-d95934717858]] and written 'Dead Pop Stars'. He left just before 'Happy Birthday' made them stars, and started over with drummer [[Steven Allen|8cd47299-26ec-4cb7-86e2-cb9ee3153b51]] and bassist Joe Donnelly.

years.src: Factory Benelux: The Wake
years.h: A home-made 45 on Scan, with a friend called Bobby on keys
years.p: With few places to play, the band paid for its own single: bright 'On Our Honeymoon' backed with the darker 'Give Up', where friend [[Bobby Gillespie|23bb4a17-70b1-4ae8-9f46-fbbfcb868b24]] plays keyboards.

years.src: Factory Benelux: The Wake · LTM: Harmony
years.h: Gillespie takes over bass from Joe Donnelly
years.p: [[Bobby Gillespie|23bb4a17-70b1-4ae8-9f46-fbbfcb868b24]] moves from guest to bassist, and Steven Allen's sister [[Carolyn Allen|b0dc65d1-7797-4c87-b253-97610da3b2aa]] joins on keyboards.

years.src: Factory Benelux: The Wake · AV Club
years.h: Gretton wants a single. The Wake makes an album
years.p: [[Rob Gretton|41b55fab-da3b-4ecf-a67d-aeeec338a9c5]] liked the demos and the Scan single and brought the band to Factory Records. At Strawberry Studios in Stockport, with engineer Chris Nagle, they cut seven tracks instead.
years.xp:
"Rob was thinking in terms of a single," Caesar said later. "But we wanted to do something lengthier while we had the opportunity."

Nagle was [[Martin Hannett|ffbfce58-5185-4bcc-8c45-a7cd5d1a3783]]'s engineer of choice and had worked on [[Joy Division|9a58fda3-f4ed-4080-a3a5-f457aac9fcdd]] and on New Order's Movement. Caesar credited his "easy-going manner, super confident technical abilities and natural quiet creativity."

years.src: Factory Benelux: The Wake · LTM: Harmony
years.h: Harmony, Fact 60, gets five stars in Sounds
years.p: A seven-track mini-album. Dave McCullough's review singled out 'Favour' as a hit single for Factory, if Factory cared to push it.
years.xp: McCullough called it "the first genuine record I can think of for months." The European pressing on Factory Benelux (FBN 29) added an eighth track, the experimental 'Chance'.

eras.title: Under New Order's wing, and in its shadow
eras.text: Dates with New Order put the Wake in front of big crowds and under a big shadow: critics kept comparing them. Gillespie left for his own band, Vini Reilly turned up on piano, and a sure-footed Island deal fell apart over who got final say.

years.src: Factory Benelux: The Wake · AV Club · Wikipedia: The Wake
years.h: On the road with New Order
years.p: Support dates with [[New Order|f1106b17-dcbb-45f6-b938-199ccfab50cc]] put the Wake in front of New Order's crowds. Critics heard the same stark romance in both bands and compared them, rarely in the Wake's favour.

q: To be fair, it's certainly no Teenage Kicks.
years.src: Factory Benelux: The Wake · LTM: Harmony
years.h: John Peel's verdict on 'Uniform'
years.p: The band's [[John Peel|e4dec348-ad10-43b6-a2b1-c22aab890675]] session has 'The Drill', 'Uniform' and 'Here Comes Everybody', Gillespie's last recordings with the Wake. Peel back-announced 'Uniform' with two words.
years.xp: Caesar took it in good humour, pointing out that 'Uniform' was no 'Teenage Kicks', the Undertones song Peel loved most. The session tracks later went onto the Harmony reissues.

years.src: Factory Benelux: The Wake · Wikipedia: The Wake
years.h: Gillespie leaves to work on Primal Scream
years.p: [[Bobby Gillespie|23bb4a17-70b1-4ae8-9f46-fbbfcb868b24]] goes off to build [[Primal Scream|55704c38-224f-4b75-b29f-d43653f8bc9a]] and drums for [[The Jesus and Mary Chain|e938a15c-b17e-4e7a-9f68-ff0d536cab44]]. Alexander 'Mac' Macpherson takes the bass.

years.src: Factory Benelux: The Wake
years.h: 'Something Outside' runs nearly eight minutes, on purpose
years.p: Cut in May at Revolution studio in Manchester and issued on Factory Benelux (FBN 24): a dubbed-out 12-inch backed with 'Host'.
years.xp: "We were a lot more confident about what we were doing by that point," Caesar said. "More confident to the point that we thought it was quite the thing to play away for nearly eight minutes per song."

years.src: Factory Benelux: The Wake · Wikipedia: The Wake
years.h: Vini Reilly plays piano on 'Talk About the Past'
years.p: Fac 88, with [[The Durutti Column|aaddb5e3-f8a5-4a9d-8674-f885112ecf0e]]'s [[Vini Reilly|f639c53e-c709-407f-9711-de495461f28d]] on piano, is the closest the Wake came to a hit: No. 11 on the UK indie chart.

years.src: Factory Benelux: The Wake
years.h: Island wants the Wake. Caesar wants final say on the sleeves
years.p: The band signs publishing with Blue Mountain Music, and its parent label Island moves to sign them. Talks break down over Caesar's demand for control of singles and artwork.

years.src: Factory Benelux: The Wake
years.h: Macpherson leaves and the Wake goes on as a trio
years.p: Alexander Macpherson quits and Caesar plays bass in the studio. In February 1985 the band finishes Scottish dates with New Order playing to a taped bass line.

years.cap: Carolyn Allen at a Yamaha DX7, c. 1985
years.src: Factory Benelux: The Wake · AV Club
years.h: Here Comes Everybody, under an El Lissitzky sleeve
years.p: Fact 130, produced by Keith 'Oz' McCormick at Revolution: 'O Pamela', 'Melancholy Man', 'All I Asked You To Do'. The AV Club later called it the band's apex.
years.xp:
Caesar wrote most of the words in the studio as the music came together. "Although the songs seem autobiographical, nearly all the situations and implied characters weren't real," he said. "I didn't know anyone called Pamela."

Carolyn Allen remembered the last night of mixing, lying on the studio couch half asleep as the songs drifted in and out: "It was so dreamlike, then emotional."

years.src: Factory Benelux: The Wake · Wikipedia: The Wake
years.h: John Leckie produces, then a sleeve fight ends Factory
years.p: Fac 178, with bassist John Rahim: shorter songs, organs and backwards parts. The band's last Factory release.
years.xp:
"John was very orientated towards the Sixties and psychedelia, into phasing and backwards parts, and organs," Caesar said. "Then a fight over the artwork made it clear that there wasn't much of a future for us at Factory."

Wikipedia adds that the band had long been unhappy with how little Factory promoted them. They left in 1988.

eras.title: Bristol, borrowed Orchids, and a label that shut itself
eras.text: The Wake landed at Sarah Records, the Bristol label of fanzine-sized pop singles, and made their brightest records with help from Glasgow's The Orchids. When Sarah closed in 1995, so did the band.

years.src: Factory Benelux: The Wake
years.h: 'Crush the Flowers' opens the Sarah years
years.p: Sarah 21: an uptempo single with Caesar and Carolyn trading vocals, and James Moody and Matthew Drummond of [[The Orchids|420d6371-31ee-4254-8d98-d3f66d50feed]] on bass and guitar.

years.src: Factory Benelux: The Wake
years.h: Make It Loud, album three, on Sarah
years.p: Sarah 602, after tours of Europe with the Orchids and of France with [[The Field Mice|7a86ff6f-cdfc-4ac3-97ca-6a48b8d1b8cd]].

years.src: Factory Benelux: The Wake · Wikipedia: The Wake
years.h: 'Major John' is Steven Allen's last record with the band
years.p: The Sarah 48 single, backed with 'Lousy Pop Group', is the drummer's final recording. Wikipedia dates his exit to 1993.

years.src: Factory Benelux: The Wake · Wikipedia: The Wake
years.h: Caesar and Carolyn make Tidal Wave of Hype as a duo
years.p: Sarah 618, with Moody, Drummond, bassist Duncan Cameron and keyboardist David McLean helping out. When Sarah closed in 1995, the Wake stopped too.

eras.title: Theatre, the Keepers and a night in Brussels
eras.text: Caesar and Carolyn didn't stop working: they made plays and records under other names while LTM put the back catalogue out on CD. A Factory tribute night in Brussels got the Wake back on stage.

years.src: Factory Benelux: The Wake
years.h: The Durutti Column plays live under Caesar's Steppenwolf
years.p: With the theatre group Twelve Stars, Caesar and Carolyn stage Treatise on the Steppenwolf in Glasgow, with [[The Durutti Column|aaddb5e3-f8a5-4a9d-8674-f885112ecf0e]] playing the soundtrack live.

years.src: Factory Benelux: The Wake · Wikipedia: The Wake
years.h: With Bobby Wratten, they become the Occasional Keepers
years.p: Caesar and Carolyn record The Beauty of the Empty Vessel for LTM with Bobby Wratten of [[The Field Mice|7a86ff6f-cdfc-4ac3-97ca-6a48b8d1b8cd]] and [[Trembling Blue Stars|59a2e877-0571-40c3-a405-2e52b170fa2c]]. True North follows in 2008.

years.cap: Caesar at Plan K, Brussels, December 12, 2009
years.src: Factory Benelux: The Wake · Wikipedia: The Wake
years.h: A Factory Night (Again) at Plan K brings the Wake back
years.p: Caesar and Carolyn play Brussels on a bill with [[A Certain Ratio|73577e86-4da8-4d76-949d-34c757e053be]] and [[Section 25|82e26f64-813d-4b22-a442-44d182f7f9eb]], with Ronnie Borland and Chris Quinn of the Orchids sitting in. London, Paris and New York follow.
years.xp: In February 2010 the band stepped in at the last minute at London Popfest at the Lexington, playing 45 minutes. They also played Indietracks in July 2013.

years.src: Factory Benelux: The Wake
years.h: Album five, 17 years after the fourth
years.p: A Light Far Out, made with Ian Catt of [[Saint Etienne|3997d4a6-c2bd-4191-8406-eb07f0abb5d2]] and Duncan Cameron, comes out on LTM; Factory Benelux presses it on vinyl in 2013.
years.xp: "Really it's been a process of rediscovery," Caesar said. He hoped it combined the old records with what he and Carolyn had done as the Occasional Keepers.

years.src: Factory Benelux: The Wake
years.h: Peter Saville letters Testament, and Gretton's tapes give up seven songs
years.p: A best-of spanning Factory and Sarah. The vinyl comes with a CD of seven lost 1981–82 songs found in [[Rob Gretton|41b55fab-da3b-4ecf-a67d-aeeec338a9c5]]'s tape archive.
